data.title: TOMI Environmental Solutions Names Srirathan as Permanent CFO
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

TOMI Environmental Solutions appointed Niroshan Srirathan as its permanent chief financial officer, elevating him from the interim role.

Srirathan's appointment is effective immediately. He was appointed the company's controller on May 4 before being named interim CFO on May 16.

He will have a base salary of $205,000 in the CFO role.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Nasdaq Plunges To One-Month Low Amid Renewed Tech Sell-Off
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After recovering from an early slump to end Thursday's session mostly higher, stocks showed a significant move back to the downside during trading on Friday. Technology stocks led the way lower, dragging the tech-heavy Nasdaq down to its lowest closing level in a month.

The Nasdaq ended the day off its lows of the session but still plunged 572.99 points or 2.1 percent to 26,140.03. The S&P 500 also slumped 84.62 points or 1.1 percent to 7,659.44, while the narrower Dow posted a more modest loss, falling 175.28 points or 0.3 percent to 52,002.41.

For the week, the Nasdaq plummeted by 4.5 percent and the S&P 500 tumbled by 2 percent, but the Dow increased by 0.7 percent.

A renewed sell-off among technology stocks weighed on the Nasdaq amid concerns about debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending.

Computer hardware stocks turned in some of the tech sector's worst performances, extending the nosedive seen over the past couple weeks, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index plummeting by 5.4 percent to a two-month closing low.

Semiconductor, networking and software also saw substantial weakness, contributing to the steep drop by the Nasdaq.

Outside of the tech sector, airline stocks moved sharply lower amid an extended surge by the price of crude oil, dragging the NYSE Arca Airline Index down by 3.2 percent.

Brokerage and biotechnology stocks also saw notable weakness, while energy stocks moved significantly higher along with the price of crude oil.

U.S. crude oil futures spiked back above $100 a barrel for the first time in a month as Iran has re-escalated its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the purported 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine has seemingly unraveled.

On the U.S. economic front, a report released by the Federal Reserve showed industrial production in the U.S. increased by more than expected in the month of September.

The Fed said industrial production climbed by 0.7 percent in September following a revised 0.1 percent uptick in August.

Economists had expected industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent compared to the unchanged reading originally reported for the previous month.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index shot up by 1.4 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index increased by 0.5 percent.

The major European markets have moved to the upside on the day. While the German DAX Index jumped by 1 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index climbed by 0.4 percent and the French CAC 40 Index rose by 0.3 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have shown a lack of direction following a recent rally. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its, is down by 1.2 basis points at 5.075 percent.

data.title: SpaceX Stocks Fall 1.94% Despite Evercore's $275 Price Target
data.description:
Space, connectivity and AI company SpaceX traded at $145.73, down 1.94%, at 11:35 a.m. ET on October 16, despite a bigger price target from Evercore ISI. According to Investing.com, the firm maintained its Outperform rating and raised its target to $275 from $230. That is a 19.6% increase in the target. The investment case now carries a higher bar for execution.

Evercore increased its 2027 computing-capacity estimate to 6.5 gigawatts from 5.7 gigawatts, a roughly 14% revision, according to the report. Separately, SpaceX's September 28 mission account says Starship Flight 14 deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Those developments measure different things. A successful satellite deployment marks progress for connectivity, but it does not establish that projected computing capacity will be financed, powered and delivered on schedule.

The valuation leaves little room for easy assumptions. The financial snapshot shows a $1.98 trillion market capitalization, a 15.09 price-to-book ratio and a GF Score of just 15 out of 100a combination that puts pressure on future execution to justify the price. Investors need evidence that computing projects can become operating capacity and that satellite deployments can generate paying usage. A higher analyst target lifts expectations. Turning those expectations into durable cash flow is the harder job.

data.title: Tech stocks drag Nasdaq 2% lower; sheds over 4% for the week
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index plunged 2.14% on Friday as technology stocks came under pressure.

Traders wrapped a mostly losing week amid a pullback in artificial intelligence-related stocks, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance.

Semiconductor stocks suffered, with Micron Technology ending 5.63% lower in the session. Advanced Micro Devices lost 5.97%, while Sandisk declined 6.85%.

The tech-heavy index was on track for its worst week since June, as per CNBC. For the week, Nasdaq lost 4.48%.

The weekly decliners, however, were led by Rocket Lab , which lost more than 25% over the week after the space launch company pushed the inaugural flight of its Neutron rocket into 2027.

Meanwhile, consumer stocks made up most of the week’s gainers amid a broader tech sell-off. Keurig Dr Pepper notched the highest gains after Piper Sandler upgraded the beverage stock to an Overweight earlier in the week.

data.title: Compass sues California's listing service over anti-competitive rules - report
data.description:
Compass has sued the California Regional Multiple Listing Service for allegedly adopting anti-competitive rules, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

The federal court suit filed in Los Angeles reportedly alleges that CRMLS's requirement that agents list homes for sale within one business day or face fines violates U.S. antitrust laws, according to the report.

CRMLS is "dictating how Compass and its agents can and cannot compete, how Compass and its agents can and cannot serve their clients, and how homeowners can and cannot market their own homes," the company reportedly said.

The listing service had sued Compass earlier this month in New York, seeking a court order in support of its listings rules. According to the listing service, Compass wants to publicly advertise homes on its platform while withholding those same listings from the shared database, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Intel Stocks Fall 3.9% as TSMC's Packaging Comments Challenge Its Expansion
data.description:
Intel, the processor and chip manufacturing group , faces fresh advanced-packaging competition, with shares at $91.61, down approximately 3.94%, at 11:17 a.m. ET on October 16. According to TipRanks, TSMC has signaled it can support customers if competing packaging capacity falls short. That raises the stakes for Intel's expansion. It does not establish that Intel has lost a customer or an order.

TSMC's earnings transcript outlines its packaging technology ambitions, underscoring the pressure Intel faces to deliver at scale. Intel's own numbers show why execution matters: its second-quarter results recorded $5.765 billion in Foundry revenue and a $2.089 billion operating loss. That puts the loss at roughly 36.2% of segment revenue. Revenue includes internal transactions, and those figures cover the broader Foundry business rather than packaging alone. Winning work is one hurdle. Making it profitable is another.

The valuation leaves little room for disappointment: Intel's $91.61 share price stands 182.92% above its $32.38 GF Value estimate. That premium suggests investors are already paying for substantial improvement, even while Foundry remains deeply unprofitable. The next test is concrete: deliver packaging milestones, convert demand into production and narrow the losses. Technology progress matters, but stronger factory economics would give the turnaround more financial weight.

data.title: Memory Chip Stocks Crashed 50% -- BofA Delivers Powerful Warning to Bears
data.description:
Bank of America sees the retreat in memory-chip shares as sharper than the industry's outlook warrants, and expects pricing and margins to remain supportive through 2028.

SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) have each lost more than 50% from June peaks. Yet based on projected 2027 and 2028 earnings, both trade at two to three times earnings, below multiples of four to seven times seen in previous memory upcycles.

BofA expects memory prices, sales and profitability to hold up over the next two years. Although 2028 earnings per share could ease by a single-digit percentage, analysts expect profits to remain near record levels.

Investors are watching SK Hynix's Oct. 28 outlook for the December quarter, which could include a special cash dividend. Taiwan's Nanya Technology has already issued a positive forecast. BofA also cited monthly PC memory contract-price increases of at least 15% and steady spot prices.

Investor views remain divided. Concerns include financing pressures among AI cloud providers, additional Chinese supply and slower AI spending, even as the bank sees fundamentals supporting the sector.

data.title: 1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown, Inc. (OTCID: FSMK) (the “Company”), parent company of 1st Summit Bank, today announced net income of $2.55 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.3% compared to $2.49 million for the second quarter of 2026 and 49.7% compared to $1.70 million for the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the first nine months of 2026 totaled $7.3 million.

Third quarter results are a continuation of the progress established earlier in the year, with strong loan growth, further expansion in net interest margin, and stable credit quality. Net interest income increased 3.4% from the prior quarter, while noninterest expense increased just 0.6%, demonstrating continued discipline as the Company grows and invests in its future.

“Our third quarter results reflect the work that we have put into strengthening 1st Summit,” said Allison Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of 1st Summit Bancorp. “During the third quarter, we grew loans at a double-digit annualized rate, maintained stable credit quality, and kept quarterly expense growth below 1%. We are particularly encouraged by our ability to grow the loan portfolio while also maintaining the strong underwriting standards that have served this Bank well.”

She continued, “The progress is visible in our results, but it begins with our people and the relationships they build every day. Our team has remained focused on understanding customers’ needs, earning their business, and managing the Bank with discipline. We believe that this commitment will continue to help us build a stronger earnings foundation while creating room to invest in the customer experience and the future of the franchise.”

Balance Sheet Growth

Gross loans increased $24.2 million during the quarter to $941.5 million at September 30, 2026, representing annualized growth of 10.47%. Loans increased $60.2 million, or 9.1% annualized, from December 31, 2025. Quarterly loan growth was led by commercial real estate and construction, land and development lending.

Total deposits increased $13.9 million to $1.19 billion at September 30, 2026, representing annualized growth of 4.68%. Growth in interest-bearing demand deposits more than offset declines in time deposits and noninterest-bearing deposits during the third quarter of 2026. The loan-to-deposit ratio increased to 79.1% at September 30, 2026, compared to approximately 78.0% at June 30, 2026, as the Company continued to improve its earning asset mix.

Management continues to view loan growth and the development of lasting deposit relationships as closely connected priorities, and that growing those relationships supports the Bank’s lending capacity and strengthens the funding foundation needed to sustain its progress.

Total assets were $1.52 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.53 billion at June 30, 2026. Shareholders’ equity totaled $99.5 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $109.9 million at June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a $12.1 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive losses. Changes in accumulated other comprehensive income are recorded within shareholders’ equity rather than current-period net income.

Net Interest Margin and Profitability

Net interest income totaled $9.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $316 thousand, or 3.4%, from the second quarter of 2026 and an increase of $1.5 million, or 19.1%, from the third quarter of 2025. Loan interest income increased $545 thousand from the prior quarter, more than offsetting lower investment income and higher total interest expense.

Net interest margin expanded to 2.63% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 2.57% for the second quarter of 2026 and 2.28% for the third quarter of 2025. The improvement reflects continued progress in shifting the earning asset mix toward loans and strengthening the Company’s underlying earnings capacity.

With the current interest rate environment and liability mix, the pace of further margin expansion will depend increasingly on continued loan growth in the fourth quarter. Management remains focused on disciplined loan pricing and developing deposit relationships that support sustainable growth.

Profitability and operating efficiency remained solid during the third quarter of 2026:

  • Annualized return on average assets was 0.66%.

  • Annualized return on average equity was 9.47%.

  • The efficiency ratio remained essentially stable at 73.64%, compared to 73.61% for the second quarter of 2026.

Credit Quality Remains Stable

Credit quality remained stable during the third quarter of 2026 as the loan portfolio grew. Nonaccrual loans represented 0.32% of total loans at September 30, 2026. The allowance for credit losses totaled $7.3 million at September 30, 2026, or 0.78% of gross loans, and covered nonaccrual loans by approximately 2.39 times. The provision for credit losses was $200 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, unchanged from the prior quarter.

Management believes this performance reinforces the value of consistent underwriting and active portfolio monitoring, and that preserving credit quality remains central to the Company’s approach to growth and its ability to translate new business into lasting shareholder value.

Noninterest Income and Expense

Noninterest income totaled $2.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decline of $251 thousand, or 10.9%, from the second quarter of 2026, primarily reflecting lower interchange and wealth management income. Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest income increased 2.9%. No gains on sales of investment securities were recognized during the quarter.

Noninterest expense totaled $8.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $51 thousand, or 0.6%, from the second quarter of 2026. Lower professional services and other operating expenses helped offset increases in salaries and benefits, data processing, and regulatory assessments and insurance.

The Company continues to manage everyday operating costs carefully while directing resources toward investments that improve service and support future growth.

Looking Forward

“We enter the final quarter of 2026 encouraged by what our team has accomplished and focused on closing out a strong year by delivering solid operating results,” Johnson concluded. “Our priorities remain clear: continue growing quality loans, build lasting deposit relationships, and preserve the discipline behind our progress. We are proud of how far we have come and remain committed to doing the work that creates long-term value for our shareholders, customers, and communities.”

About 1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown, Inc.

1st Summit, through its wholly owned subsidiary, 1st Summit Bank (the “Bank”), is a community oriented financial institution that primarily focuses on relationship banking for both consumers and businesses. From 17 full-service community offices and one loan production office, the Bank provides a full array of personal and business banking solutions, investment management and trust services. The Bank serves communities throughout the counties of Cambria, Westmoreland, Blair, Somerset, and Indiana. Please visit Home | 1st Summit Bank for more information.

data.title: ASND Shares Shrug Off Positive European Opinion For FDA-Approved Achondroplasia Drug
data.description:
Key points:
  • Final European Commission authorization is still pending, with a decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a potential first launch in Germany in the first quarter of 2027.
  • Ascendis has three approved commercial products.
  • TransCon CNP, marketed as YUVIWEL in the U.S., received FDA approval in February 2026.

Ascendis Pharma (ASND) said on Friday that it has received a positive European regulatory opinion for its once-weekly treatment for children with achondroplasia.

Shares of the company closed down 0.6%, as investors likely viewed the positive opinion as expected, provided it is already approved in the U.S. TransCon CNP, marketed as YUVIWEL in the U.S., received FDA approval in February 2026 to increase linear growth in children two years and older with open growth plates.

CHMP Opinion On Ascendis Drug

Ascendis said the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use adopted a positive opinion on Ascendis’s application seeking approval for the drug in achondroplasia for children two years of age and older whose epiphyses, or the expanded end of a long bone, are not closed.

The opinion followed review of data from three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials plus up to three years of open-label extension results, including the pivotal ApproaCH trial. Final European Commission authorization is still pending, with a decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a potential first launch in Germany in the first quarter of 2027.

Chief Executive Officer Jan Mikkelsen said the positive opinion reflects the unique profile of TransCon CNP and that the therapy remains a foundational product in the company’s growth disorder portfolio supporting its longer-term objectives.

Ascendis has three approved commercial products, including TransCon CNP. In the second quarter, or its first quarter of commercial sales, the drug recorded €7.6–8 million in revenue, accounting for a small portion of the company’s overall product revenue of €315 million. YORVIPATH accounts for a lion’s share of the company’s overall sales.

How Did ASND Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ASND stock stayed within bearish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed within normal levels.

ASND stock has gained 6% year-to-date.

data.description:
(TheNewswire)

VANCOUVER, BC – TheNewswire – October 16, 2026 - GOLD’N FUTURES MINERAL CORP. (FSE: G6M) (the “Company” or “Gold’n Futures”) is pleased to announce the appointment of Curtis Riou as Chief Executive Officer and as a director of the Company, effective immediately.

Mr. Riou is a Professional Geoscientist with more than 25 years of experience in environmental consulting and resource development across Canada's oil, gas and mining sectors. He serves as Chief Operating Officer of Apex Exploration Corp. and is a co-founder of X-Terra Environmental Services Ltd., a First Nation–owned environmental consulting firm.

His background combines project management with environmental and regulatory expertise, bringing a practical perspective to the planning and oversight of resource projects.

The Company also announces that Khaled Hatabah has resigned as Chief Executive Officer and as a director of the Company, effective immediately.

The board of directors welcomes Mr. Riou and looks forward to working with him as the Company enters a new chapter. The Company also thanks Mr. Hatabah for his contributions and service and wishes him well in his future endeavours.

data.title: Seagate Stocks Fall 5.34%; Target Cut Puts Cash Generation Under Scrutiny
data.description:
Hard-drive manufacturer Seagate fell to $653.95, down approximately 5.34%, at 11:35 a.m. ET on October 16 as investors digested a steep analyst target cut. TipRanks reported that Wells Fargo lowered its target to $865 from $1,180, a reduction of roughly 27%. That puts cash generation under the spotlight: can Seagate keep turning booming storage demand into money shareholders can count?

The business enters that test with substantial cash flow behind it. Seagate's July 28 results showed $3.1 billion in fiscal-year free cash flow on $12.195 billion in revenue, implying a margin of about 25.4%. Year-end debt stood at $3.6 billion against $1.7 billion in cash. Management guided fiscal-first-quarter revenue to $4.0 billion$4.2 billion. The next report will test whether that growth also delivers strong margins and cash conversion.

The valuation panel shows Seagate trading 229.55% above its $198.44 GF Value estimate, leaving a substantial premium that future performance must justify. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a prediction of where shares will trade. A lower analyst target alone does not establish deteriorating operations. The sharper question is whether Seagate can defend its cash-flow margin as capacity expands. More storage sold helps shareholders most when pricing and investment spending leave plenty of cash behind.

data.title: Palantir Stocks Fall 6.6% Although Mizuho Raises Target to $245
data.description:
Enterprise-AI software provider Palantir faces a tougher test than a higher analyst target can settle, with shares at $187.325, down approximately 6.57%, around 11:35 a.m. ET on October 16. According to The Fly, Mizuho analyst Gregg Moskowitz lifted his target to $245 from $215 while keeping an Outperform rating. That is a roughly 14% increase in the target. The question for shareholders is how much operating progress survives the adjustments.

Palantir's August 3 earnings release puts second-quarter GAAP operating profit at $912 million, compared with $1.194 billion on an adjusted basis. The $282.5 million gap consists of $265.2 million in stock-based compensation and $17.3 million in related employer payroll taxes. Those exclusions account for 23.6% of adjusted operating profit. The business is profitable under both measures, but shareholders should still count the cost of compensation paid in equity.

The valuation graphic shows shares just 0.13% above the $187.08 GF Value estimate, suggesting little discount to that benchmark despite the day's selloff. That estimate is a reference point, not a price floor. The next earnings report needs to show whether GAAP operating profit can grow faster than the diluted share count. Stock compensation avoids an immediate cash payment, but it can spread future earnings across more shares. A higher target strengthens the bullish narrative; stronger earnings per share would give it firmer backing.

data.title: Tesla, SpaceX, CoreWeave, Lam Research, Netflix, Strategy, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover, Mariapaula Gonzalez, and Ty Roush

Stocks fell Friday on an extended selloff in chip stocks.

Stocks had traded mixed earlier after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh offered little insight about inflation, strengthening hopes the central bank will keep interest rates unchanged.

Tesla fell 1.1% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled its new Roadster sports car. The car's SpaceX thrusters will enable it to hover in the air. SpaceX declined 1.6%.

CoreWeave plunged 11% as investors continued to fret about artificial-intelligence spending. Shares have slumped 24% this week as yields on CoreWeave's debt have soared.

Concerns about AI spending weighed on chip-equipment makers. KLA fell 2.8% and Lam Research dropped 3.1%, putting both stocks on pace for their 10th consecutive daily decline — their longest losing streaks on record. Applied Materials declined 3%.

Apple rose 0.7%. Preorders for the company's iPhone Duo started Friday, but delivery times were scheduled for the end of January, signaling strong demand for Apple's first foldable phone.

Twilio dropped 10% as shares paced toward their largest percentage decrease since August 2025.

Strategy fell 8.3% after MSCI approved new rules that could exclude the Bitcoin investor and other companies with mainly nonoperating assets from its global equity indexes starting Nov. 30.

Netflix slid 2.4% after the video streamer said Peter Rice would replace Bela Bajaria as its chief content officer, effective Oct. 26. Netflix has struggled to ease worries about declining engagement this year.

Travelers rose 0.4%. The company posted fiscal third-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street's estimates, while also reporting a year-over-year increase in its catastrophe losses.

Semtech fell 3%. Its 2030 revenue targets signaled a growth slowdown that disappointed investors, even as Wall Street still views the global semiconductor as a key AI infrastructure winner.

Alcoa rose 6.4% after the aluminum producer's third-quarter earnings beat analysts' expectations, thanks to the run-up in commodity prices.

J.B. Hunt Transport Services declined 2.4% after the trucking company narrowly beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings target. Shares were still reeling after CFO Brad Delco told investors J.B. Hunt's profit would slump between 5% and 10% due to higher fuel prices.

data.title: Wall Street ends down sharply, worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chips, AI infrastructure companies fall as debt concerns linger
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq suffer steepest weekly losses since June
  • Tesla dips after unveiling electric sports car
  • S&P 500 -1.09%, Nasdaq -2.15%, Dow -0.34%

By Noel Randewich

Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

The Nasdaq extended losses from earlier in the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom fell 4.5%, and the PHLX chip index sank 3.8% in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008.

Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries.

"There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in ​Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk."

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The S&P 500 declined 1.09% to end the session at 7,659.44 points.

The Nasdaq declined 2.15% to 26,140.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.34% to 52,002.41 points.

Reflecting a rotation from tech stocks into other areas of the stock market, six of the S&P 500's 11 sector indexes rose, led by energy , up 2.47%, followed by a 1.4% gain in utilities .

Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 18.6 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.7 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell almost 1.95% and the Nasdaq slumped 4.48%, their deepest weekly declines since June. The Dow climbed 0.67% for the week.

Third-quarter earnings season shifts into high gear next week with reports from Tesla , Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging more than 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data.

While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday voiced optimism about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

Tesla dropped 3.1% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares dipped 2.8%.

Declining stocks roughly matched rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX)..

The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 51 new highs and 353 new lows.
